AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: IL-35 is a novel cytokine suppressing the immune response through the expansion of regulatory T cells and suppression of Th17 cell development. Few studies have been done on the effect of this cytokine in a different disease. Asthma is a complex disease that many inflammatory cells and cytokines play a role in.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: We decide to determine the difference between serum level of IL-35 in childhood asthma & healthy children.

AbstractText.Label: METHOD
AbstractText.content: We obtained serum samples from 44 asthmatic children between 2 and 15 years as a case group and from healthy children as a control group. IL-35 serum concentration was determined by ELISA method in both groups.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Mean serum level is 30.9 pg/ml in the case group and 30.2 pg/ml in the control group. There is no significant difference between serum level of IL-35 in asthmatic & healthy children.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Our data reveal no relation between childhood asthma and serum level of IL35. So, further study will be needed to clarify effects of this cytokine in human allergic diseases.
